title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: What Is Information Retrieval (IR)
summary: Information Retrieval (IR) is the science of finding material — typically documents — that satisfies an information need from within large collections.

title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Boolean Retrieval Model
summary: The Boolean retrieval model matches documents against Boolean expressions of query terms using AND, OR, NOT operators. A document is either relevant (1) or not (0) — no ranking.

title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Vector Space Model — TF-IDF & Cosine Similarity
summary: The Vector Space Model (VSM) represents documents and queries as vectors in a high-dimensional term space (one dimension per unique vocabulary term). Each dimension's value is the TF-IDF weight of the corresponding term.

title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Probabilistic Retrieval Model
summary: The probabilistic retrieval model formalises relevance as a probability. Given query Q, the goal is to estimate P(R=1 | D, Q) — the probability that document D is relevant to query Q.

title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Language Model for IR — Query Likelihood
summary: The Language Model (LM) approach to IR treats each document as a probability distribution over words — a language model θ_D.

title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Bag-of-Words Assumption
summary: The bag-of-words (BoW) assumption treats a document as an unordered multiset of terms — word order and grammatical structure are discarded.

title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: IR Evaluation Framework
summary: IR evaluation requires a test collection: a document corpus, a set of queries (topics), and relevance judgements (qrels) — human-annotated labels indicating which documents are relevant to each query.

title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: TF-IDF — Deep Dive

summary: Graph RAG (Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation) augments LLM generation by retrieving context from a structured knowledge graph rather than (or in addition to) a flat vector index.

title: 08. GraphRAG: Knowledge Graph Construction
summary: Entity extraction is the process of identifying and classifying named entities (people, organisations, locations, products, concepts) in unstructured text — the first step in building a knowledge graph.

title: 08. GraphRAG: Graph Data Structures for RAG
summary: The property graph model is the dominant data structure for Graph RAG systems.

title: 08. GraphRAG: Graph Databases for Graph RAG
summary: Graph databases store, query, and traverse graph-structured data natively — unlike relational databases that require expensive JOIN operations for relationship traversal.

title: 08. GraphRAG: Community Detection Algorithms
summary: Community detection partitions a graph into clusters (communities) of nodes that are more densely connected internally than externally.

title: 08. GraphRAG: Graph Traversal & Retrieval
summary: Graph traversal is the mechanism by which Graph RAG retrieves relevant context from a knowledge graph given a query.

title: 08. GraphRAG: Hybrid Graph-Vector Retrieval
summary: Hybrid Graph-Vector Retrieval fuses two complementary retrieval signals: vector similarity (semantic closeness in embedding space) and graph traversal (structural relatedness via typed relationships).

title: 08. GraphRAG: Entity Linking & Disambiguation
summary: Entity Linking (EL) — also called Named Entity Disambiguation (NED) — is the process of mapping entity mentions in text to specific entries in a knowledge base.

title: 08. GraphRAG: Graph Query Languages
summary: Graph databases use specialised query languages designed for traversing relationships efficiently. Cypher (Neo4j) uses a declarative, ASCII-art pattern syntax ((n)-[:REL]->(m)) that is highly readable and optimised for property graphs.

title: 08. GraphRAG: Microsoft GraphRAG Deep Dive
summary: Microsoft GraphRAG (released 2024) is an end-to-end framework that constructs a hierarchical community graph from source documents, then uses that graph for both local (entity-centric) and global (theme-level) question answering.

title: 08. GraphRAG: LightRAG
summary: LightRAG (University of Hong Kong, 2024) is a Graph RAG framework designed for efficiency and simplicity while supporting both entity-level and relationship-level retrieval.
